parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the number of protons and the number of neutrons in a nucleus of $X$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why the energy transferred to the $\alpha$-particle as kinetic energy is less than the $5.5\text{ MeV}$ of energy released in the decay process.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: A sample of $X$ is used to produce a beam of $\alpha$-particles in a vacuum. The number of $\alpha$-particles passing a fixed point in the beam in a time of $30\text{ s}$ is $6.9 \times 10^{11}$.
parts.text: Calculate the average current produced by the beam of $\alpha$-particles.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the total power, in W, that is produced by the decay of $6.9 \times 10^{11}$ nuclei of $X$ in a time of $30\text{ s}$.

stem: A stationary nucleus of a radioactive isotope $X$ decays by emitting an $\alpha$-particle to produce a nucleus of neptunium-237 and $5.5\text{ MeV}$ of energy. The decay is represented by $$X \rightarrow ^{237}_{93}\text{Np} + \alpha + 5.5\text{ MeV}.$$
